ns2:section.sectionText: Over 99% of all the species that have ever lived on Earth are now extinct. Paleobiology draws from biology, geology, and paleontology to understand fossils and fossil communities as lived in the past, and seeks to answer questions about evolution, ecology, and ancient environments. In this course we will learn about myriad fossil species from the geologic record and what they can tell us about the history of life on Earth. These include: the classification and characteristics of major phyla, how fossils inform our understanding of evolution, speciation and extinction in deep time, the interactions between Earth’s climate and life, and the reconstruction of ancient communities from the fossil record. Laboratory exercises will focus on fossil collections and published datasets to provide a broad understanding of fossils and the methods we use to study them.
